newsitem.title: DENMARK: Virgin Express might contract out cargo space.
newsitem.headline: Virgin Express might contract out cargo space.

text.p: Brussels-based short-haul passenger carrier Virgin Express said on Tuesday that it might lease its cargo capability to a specialist operator.

"We currently do not carry cargo because it slows us down in our turnarounds and it's just not a business that we're familiar enough with at this time," CEO Jonathan Ornstein told a news conference promoting the airline's new Brussels-Copenhagen link.

"What we probably would look to do would potentially be to find a cargo operator and sell him our entire cargo hold and let him invest in the infrastructure and the airport operations and just pay us a fee to use our cargo space," he added.
Virgin Express, part of British entrepreneur Richard Branson's Virgin group, currently operates 14 Boeing 737 passenger aircraft and says it sees it fleet doubling over the next three years.
Ornstein said that a modular cargo operation was an option.

"We might start a 'quick-pack' operation which is similar to some of the short-haul carriers in the US. Again, you don't delay flights, because passengers are our primary concern and you find often with cargo you delay flights and it has an impact on the rest of the system," he said. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom 45- 33969650
